2. Appeal has been preferred by the aggrieved appellant - husband against the judgment dated 30.07.2016 and decree dated 05.08.2016 passed in Original Suit (M.T.S) No. 108/2013 by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Ranchi, whereby the suit preferred under section 13(1) (i-a)
(i-b) read with section 25 and 27 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 by the Respondent-wife for dissolution of marriage has been allowed with a direction to the Respondent- husband, appellant herein, to return the motorcycle and washing machine and further to pay Rs. 8.50 lakh as permanent alimony and on failure to pay the same, compound interest @ 7.5% per annum shall have to be paid.
Litigation cost of Rs. 10,000/- was also awarded.
3. During pendency of this appeal, parties have arrived at an amicable settlement during mediation at JHALSA.
Settlement was brought on record by way of a supplementary affidavit.

Order dated 27.02.2020 takes into account the settlement arrived at between the parties and the terms and conditions which the parties were supposed to comply which included disposal of pending proceedings i.e. Complaint Case No. 1774/2007 pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi and Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 08/2017 pending before the learned Family Court, Ranchi instituted by the wife.

Cr. Revision No. 319/2014 preferred by the wife being aggrieved by the order refusing maintenance to her while granting maintenance to the child, was disposed of in the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties during mediation.

Having taken into account the terms of settlement, this court vide order dated 27.02.2020 observed that if the two cases mentioned above are disposed of or withdrawn in the light of settlement by the Sanjay Kumar vs Poonam Priya on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56612837/
1 Respondent-wife and the demand draft of Rs. 8.60 lakh drawn in her favour is disbursed on the next date, appeals can be disposed of in the light of the settlement.
4. Matter has thereafter been taken up on 03.01.2022 at the instance of the Respondent.

It was informed that Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 08/2017 instituted by the Respondent before the learned Family Court, Ranchi has been withdrawn; an application for withdrawal of Complaint Case No. 1774/2007 pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi would also be filed within a week.

The office note also indicates that an amount of Rs. 8.60 lakhs through a demand draft in favour of the Respondent was deposited by the appellant in the office of learned Registrar General of this Court on 08.12.2021.

Subsequently, on 22.02.2022, this court was informed that the appellant has filed a Criminal Miscellaneous Petition under section 482 of the Cr. P.C before this Court for quashing of the entire criminal proceeding arising out of Complaint Case No. 1774/2007 as the case is non-compoundable in nature under section 498A of the I.P.C.

The appellant also stated that he would have no objection to disbursal of demand draft of Rs. 8.60 lakh if the Respondent give an assurance that she would fully cooperate and file a joint affidavit for disposal of Criminal Miscellaneous Petition preferred by the appellant.

On the assurance that the Respondent shall cooperate in the disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous Petition, this Court allowed the Respondent to seek disbursal of the demand draft of Rs. 8.60 lakh from the learned Registrar General on proper identification.

5. When the matter has been taken up today, learned counsel for the Respondent-wife submits that an amount of Rs. 8.60 lakh through a demand draft has already been disbursed in favour of the Respondent; Criminal Miscellaneous Petition No. 554/2022 has also been disposed of on 04.05.2022 in terms of the settlement.
As such, there are no lis pending between the parties except the present one.
Since the parties are living separately and their dispute has also been resolved during mediation, both the appeals may be disposed of in the light of the settlement.

6. On the basis of conspectus of facts and circumstances and developments, as taken note above, it appears that the Respondent-wife had already got the decree of divorce from the learned Family Court, Ranchi and these two appeals had been preferred by the aggrieved husband.

However, during pendency of these appeals, since the parties have arrived at an amicable settlement of the dispute and terms of the settlement has also been worked out and payment of permanent alimony has been made in favour of the Respondent, there is no lis left to be decided.
Accordingly, appeals are disposed of in terms of the settlement.
Decree accordingly.
Let the settlement form part of the decree in both appeals.

(Aparesh Kumar Singh, A.C.J) (Deepak Roshan, J) Ranjeet/
